decisions.reason: Evaluated on finding-specific empirical scope rather than citation placement, method differences, or extension wording, Carroll et al. (2022; 10.1002/jaba.908) do not empirically retest a specific finding of Parsons and Reid (1995; 10.1901/jaba.1995.28-317; verified via primary publisher abstract, full body unavailable). Parsons and Reid (1995) tested (1) whether training 10 residential supervisors solely to implement teaching programs sufficed to improve their feedback to staff (it did not), (2) subsequent 8-hr classroom plus on-the-job feedback-skills training for supervisors, and (3) comparative maintenance of already-trained teaching skills in direct-service staff whose supervisors received feedback training relative to staff whose supervisors did not. In Carroll et al. (2022), Study 1 directly replicates Shuler and Carroll (2019; 10.1007/s40617-018-00314-5, shipped row 800), which is the proximate chain target for training supervisors' 8-step feedback accuracy via brief video modeling with voiceover instructions (VMVO). Study 2 extends Shuler and Carroll (2019) by testing whether post-session feedback alone from three VMVO-trained supervisors teaches initial acquisition of a 10-step guided-compliance protocol to three previously untrained therapists in a multiple-baseline design. Neither Study 1 nor Study 2 tests the insufficiency of teaching-skill training for supervisors or comparative maintenance of previously acquired staff skills against an untrained-supervisor control.
